_about: Defaults for one developer or agency. Copy to profile.local.json (git ignores it) and fill it in. The skill reads it at intake; the site's own answers win.
developer: Your name (test leads are named 'TEST <developer> - please ignore')
_level_about: "new": plain words, every term explained once, exact clicks, the "Next:" line in plain words at the end of each stop report. "developer": short and technical.
_oks_about: "group": one OK covers a listed batch of downloads and installs, each named with its source and size. "each": every download and install is asked on its own. Deletes and live steps are always asked one at a time.
reply_style: One step at a time for manual steps; wait for 'done'.

local_admin._about: The default admin for LOCAL sites only. install-wp.py reads it in P1 setup (local URLs and WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE local only), passes the password to PHP through the environment and never prints it. This file is never committed (.gitignore). Live sites get their own strong password, typed by the developer.

local._about: Where WordPress runs on this computer. Leave it empty: doctor.py finds your local tool (Laragon, XAMPP, MAMP, WampServer, Local, Herd, DDEV, wp-env or a native setup) and fills this in with your OK.

host._about: Where sites go live. cPanel with Duplicator Pro is the kit's default; other hosts work too (references/launch.md).

tracking.method: GTM container in the head and the noscript after <body>

_extra_plugins_about: Plugins of your own or your agency's, on top of the kit's defaults (ACF PRO, Contact Form 7, Yoast SEO everywhere; Redirection when the site has redirects; Duplicator Pro for the move, deleted after live QA; Converter for Media, Contact Form CFDB7 and the cache plugin on live only). "required": true = must be there and active wherever it goes. "where": "live" = live only: installed at launch, on the live plugin checklist (RUNBOOK section 4), never local or staging; "all" (the default for a required one) = installed in P1 setup with the starter plugins and kept active on live. Without either, it is installed when its "when" says. Never installed without an OK. "slug" = its folder name in wp-content/plugins (plugin-check.py matches by it, else by the name); "zip" = its key in plugin_zips (installed only from your plugin folder); "live_note" = one line for that checklist. A tracking plugin named in tracking.plugin is the only tracking: no tracking fields or GTM in the theme.

extra_plugins.name: Your agency's plugin
extra_plugins.source: where it comes from (a zip path, or the developer installs it)

plugin_zips._about: Your plugin folder: paths on this machine to plugin zips you bought or own, keyed by a short name (acf_pro, duplicator_pro, and any of yours that extra_plugins names in "zip"). The only source for these plugins; plugin-versions.py shows each zip's version before go-live. duplicator_pro: P1 setup installs Duplicator Pro from it (for the moves to staging and live); empty = you install it before the first package. Paths only: never licence keys here.

_cache_plugin_about: The cache plugin on live (on the live plugin checklist; never staging or local). Empty = LiteSpeed Cache. Name another when the host needs it (LiteSpeed Cache page cache needs a LiteSpeed server or QUIC.cloud).
_acf_pro_license_about: Optional: your ACF PRO licence key, typed by you. make-wp-config.py writes it into LOCAL wp-config files only (ACF PRO then activates itself); never printed, never on live unless you choose. Empty = you paste it per site.

branding._about: Agency badge in the footer of the lead email AND the auto-reply (both use the same branded HTML template). A PNG at 2x size (email clients do not show SVG or WebP); a white badge sits on the brand-colour footer strip. Path relative to the skill folder or absolute; empty = no badge.
branding._site_badge_about: The same badge for the site footer's bottom bar (SVG is fine on the web): kitwp_agency_badge(). Theme Settings > Branding can swap or hide it.

leads_portal._about: Optional, none by default: leave constant_prefix empty and leads go by email and CFDB7 only (no Theme Settings group, no runbook item, nothing blocks). Fill constant_prefix to turn on your leads portal: every lead form then also goes there server to server (JSON, Bearer key), also when the email fails; its address and password go into Theme Settings > Leads portal on live (administrators only; the developer pastes them; stored in the database, so they travel in packages and backups); wp-config constants <constant_prefix>_ENDPOINT and <constant_prefix>_KEY win when defined. Off on local, development and staging. A site can opt out: site.json "leads_portal": "none: <reason>". admin: the portal admin URL; setup: how a project is made.
